tooltips.kill_switch_detailed: When the VPN connection drops, all internet traffic is blocked to prevent your data from leaking outside the VPN. Recommended to keep enabled for maximum security. Enabled Kill Switch may slightly slow down VPN connection.
tooltips.anti_dpi_detailed: Disguises VPN traffic as regular HTTPS to bypass Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) systems used by ISPs and government agencies to block VPNs.
tooltips.post_quantum_detailed: Uses encryption algorithms resistant to quantum computer attacks. Protects your data from future decryption. Slightly increases connection time.
tooltips.ipv6_detailed: Allows IPv6 traffic routing through the VPN tunnel. If your ISP or server doesn't support IPv6, keep this disabled to avoid connection issues.
tooltips.dns_upstreams: Custom DNS servers for queries through VPN. Multiple servers work as fallbacks: if the first doesn't respond, the next is used. Encrypted protocols DoT, DoH, DoQ are supported to protect DNS queries from ISP interception.
tooltips.mtu: MTU size (576–9000). Lower values are more reliable on poor connections, higher values improve throughput.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.hint_dns: The DNS record (A record) for the domain does not point to the server IP address. Add an A record in your domain control panel and wait 5–10 minutes.
error.hint_letsencrypt: Let's Encrypt could not issue a certificate. Make sure the domain points to the server and port 80 is open.
error.hint_port_in_use: Port 443 is already in use by another process. Open a terminal on the server and check who's listening: sudo ss -tlnp | grep :443 — then stop that service or use a separate VPS.
error.hint_port_held_by: Port 443 is held by «{{process}}» — TrustTunnel cannot run alongside it. Options: stop «{{process}}» (sudo systemctl stop {{process}}), move it to another port, or use a separate VPS for TrustTunnel.
error.hint_port_80: Port 80 must be open and not occupied by another service (nginx, apache) to obtain a certificate.
error.hint_port_80_busy: Port 80 is occupied by another web server, so Let's Encrypt could not issue a certificate. The fastest fix is to switch to a self-signed certificate: the install completes immediately, with no dependency on port 80.
error.hint_port_80_refused: Your VPS replied «Connection refused» on port 80 — the packet got through, but nothing is listening. Likely nginx/apache holds 443 with no forward on 80. Before certbot: sudo systemctl stop nginx (or apache2), then retry. After certbot succeeds you can bring nginx back up.
error.hint_port_80_timeout: Let's Encrypt's external probe to your VPS on port 80 timed out — a firewall is dropping inbound packets. Check: (1) sudo ufw allow 80/tcp on the server, (2) iptables -L INPUT, (3) Inbound rules in your VPS provider panel (AWS Security Group / DigitalOcean / Selectel — port 80/tcp must be open for 0.0.0.0/0). This is NOT a Let's Encrypt rate limit — it's the server being unreachable from the internet.
error.hint_unreachable: Server unreachable. Verify the IP address is correct, the server is running and not blocking connections from your network.
error.hint_auth_failed: SSH authentication error. Check your username and password.
error.hint_config_diverges: This is not an install error: the server still has a config from a previous version. «Reinstall» will overwrite it with your settings, while users and their passwords are preserved.
